stem: A registered representative is charged with a felony. Within what time frame must the Form U4 be amended?

choices.text: 10 days
30 days after learning of the facts
Only upon conviction
At the next annual compliance meeting

spoken_stem: A registered rep is charged with a felony. How soon must the Form U4 be amended? A, ten days. B, thirty days after learning of the facts. C, only once convicted. D, at the next annual compliance meeting.
explanation: B is correct. Under the FINRA By-Laws, Article V, Form U4 must be kept current, and amendments must be filed no later than 30 days after learning of the facts or circumstances. Felony charges are reportable on the U4 even before a conviction, so C is wrong. A is not the general U4 deadline. D is far too late.
spoken_explanation: B, within thirty days. Felony charges must be reported on the U4, not just convictions, and amendments are due within thirty days of learning the facts. Other U4 events include customer complaints, liens, bankruptcies, regulatory actions and changes of address. Willfully filing false or incomplete information can itself be grounds for discipline.

stem: When a registered representative leaves a firm, the firm must file a Form U5:

choices.text: Within 10 days and send a copy to FINRA only
Within 30 days of termination and provide a copy to the individual
Within 90 days, but only if the termination was for cause
Only if the rep joins another FINRA firm

spoken_stem: When a rep leaves a firm, when must the firm file Form U5? A, within ten days, copy to FINRA only. B, within thirty days of termination, with a copy to the rep. C, within ninety days, only if fired for cause. D, only if the rep joins another FINRA firm.
explanation: B is correct. Form U5 must be filed within 30 days after termination, for any reason, and the firm must give the individual a copy within the same period. It discloses the reason for leaving and any reportable events. A has the wrong deadline and omits the copy. C is wrong: every termination requires a U5. D is wrong: it's required regardless of where the rep goes.
spoken_explanation: B. Thirty days after anyone leaves, for any reason, the firm files the U5 and gives the rep a copy. If the U5 shows a termination for cause, it shows up on BrokerCheck and future employers will see it, so firms must be accurate. Misstatements can lead to defamation claims and FINRA discipline.

stem: Which of the following would generally cause a statutory disqualification under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934?

choices.text: A speeding ticket two years ago
A felony conviction within the past 10 years
A personal bankruptcy filing six years ago
A customer complaint that was settled for $5,000

spoken_stem: Which would generally cause a statutory disqualification? A, a speeding ticket two years ago. B, a felony conviction within the last ten years. C, a personal bankruptcy six years ago. D, a customer complaint settled for five thousand.
explanation: B is correct. Exchange Act Section 3(a)(39) includes any felony conviction within the past 10 years, as well as certain securities- or money-related misdemeanors, SRO expulsions and certain regulatory orders. C and D are reportable on Form U4 in many cases but are not statutory disqualifications. A is not reportable or disqualifying.
spoken_explanation: B, a felony in the last ten years. Bankruptcies and settled complaints get disclosed on the U4, but they don't automatically disqualify you. A statutorily disqualified person can only stay in the industry if the firm applies and FINRA approves continued association, usually with heightened supervision.

stem: Under FINRA Rule 1240, how often must a registered person complete the Regulatory Element of continuing education?

choices.text: Every 3 years after registration
Annually, by December 31
Only on the 2nd, 5th and 10th registration anniversaries
Only when switching firms

spoken_stem: Under FINRA Rule twelve forty, how often must a registered person complete the Regulatory Element of C E? A, every three years. B, every year by December thirty-first. C, only at the second, fifth and tenth anniversaries. D, only when switching firms.
explanation: B is correct. Since January 1, 2023, the Regulatory Element must be completed annually, by December 31 of each year, with content tailored to the person's registrations. Missing it makes the person CE-inactive. A and C reflect the old anniversary-based schedule. D isn't a trigger. The Firm Element, the firm's own annual training, is separate.
spoken_explanation: B, every year by December thirty-first. The old schedule of second, fifth and tenth anniversaries ended in twenty twenty-three. The Firm Element is the firm's own yearly training, and it's separate. Persons who leave the industry can keep their qualifications alive for up to five years through the Maintaining Qualifications Program, by completing annual CE.

stem: A sales assistant who is NOT registered may do which of the following?

choices.text: Accept an unsolicited order from a customer when the rep is out
Make cold calls to schedule appointments for the rep, without discussing investments
Receive a share of commissions on trades they processed
Recommend money market funds to customers

spoken_stem: A sales assistant who is NOT registered may do which of these? A, take an unsolicited order when the rep is out. B, cold-call to set appointments, without discussing investments. C, get a share of commissions on trades they handled. D, recommend money market funds.
explanation: B is correct. Unregistered persons may do clerical and ministerial tasks, including calls only to set appointments or qualify leads, as long as they don't discuss investments. A is wrong: taking orders requires registration. C violates FINRA Rule 2040, which bars paying transaction-based compensation to unregistered persons. D is a recommendation, and that requires registration.
spoken_explanation: B. An unregistered assistant can set appointments but can't take orders, can't make recommendations, and can't be paid commissions. Rule twenty-forty also bars paying transaction-based compensation to any unregistered person, including finders, unless an exception applies. A good test: if the task involves investment advice, accepting orders, or getting paid per trade, registration is required.

stem: Under FINRA Rule 3270, a registered rep who wants to take a paid weekend job as a real estate agent must:

choices.text: Do nothing, since the job is unrelated to securities
Provide prior written notice to the member firm
Obtain FINRA's prior written approval
Notify the firm within 30 days after starting

spoken_stem: Under FINRA Rule thirty-two seventy, a rep wants a paid weekend job as a real estate agent. What must she do? A, nothing, it's unrelated to securities. B, give her firm prior written notice. C, get FINRA's prior approval. D, tell the firm within thirty days after starting.
explanation: B is correct. Rule 3270 requires prior written notice to the firm before engaging in any outside business activity for compensation, even one unrelated to securities. The firm then assesses it and may restrict or prohibit it. A is wrong because unrelated paid work still counts. C is wrong: notice goes to the firm, not FINRA. D is after the fact. Note: the SEC approved new FINRA Rule 3290 in September 2026, consolidating Rules 3270 and 3280 and effective October 25, 2027. Until then, 3270 applies.
spoken_explanation: B, prior written notice to her firm. Any paid outside work counts, even outside securities. Heads up: FINRA's new Rule thirty-two ninety replaces thirty-two seventy and thirty-two eighty in October twenty twenty-seven. Passive investments, like buying stock in a company, generally don't count as an outside business activity, but private securities transactions are covered by a different rule.

stem: A rep wants to sell interests in a friend's private real estate venture, away from her firm, and will receive a commission. Under FINRA Rule 3280, which is required?

choices.text: Written notice only; no approval needed
Prior written notice, and the firm's written approval, with the firm recording and supervising the trade as its own
FINRA approval and a Form U4 amendment
Nothing, since private placements are exempt from registration

spoken_stem: A rep wants to sell interests in a friend's private real estate deal, away from her firm, for a commission. Under Rule thirty-two eighty, what's required? A, written notice only. B, prior written notice and the firm's written approval, with the firm recording and supervising it as its own. C, FINRA approval and a U4 amendment. D, nothing, private placements are exempt.
explanation: B is correct. A private securities transaction for compensation requires prior written notice describing the deal and the rep's role. The firm must approve or disapprove in writing. If approved, it records the transaction on its books and supervises it as its own. If there's no compensation, written notice is required and the firm may require more. A applies to uncompensated transactions. C isn't the mechanism. D confuses issuer registration exemptions with the rep's conduct obligations. Rule 3290 will replace Rule 3280 effective October 25, 2027.
spoken_explanation: B. Selling away for pay needs written notice, then the firm's written approval, and then the firm books and supervises it like its own business. Without pay, written notice is the minimum. Selling away without telling the firm is one of the most common reasons reps get barred. Investors who lose money often try to hold the firm responsible.

stem: As of 2026, under FINRA Rule 3220, a rep may give a gift to an employee of a client institution, in relation to that institution's business, worth no more than:

choices.text: $50 per person per year
$100 per person per year
$300 per person per year
$500 per person per year

spoken_stem: As of twenty twenty-six, under FINRA Rule thirty-two twenty, what's the most a rep can give as a gift to an employee of a client institution, in relation to that business? A, fifty dollars a year. B, one hundred a year. C, three hundred a year. D, five hundred a year.
explanation: C is correct. FINRA raised the Rule 3220 gift limit from $100 to $300 per person per year, effective March 30, 2026 (Regulatory Notice 26-05). MSRB Rule G-20 followed for FINRA-member dealers on June 1, 2026. B was the limit from 1992 until March 2026, and exam prep material written earlier may still show $100. Ordinary business entertainment where the rep attends isn't counted toward the gift limit, though gifts given at the event are. A and D are not the limits.
spoken_explanation: C, three hundred dollars per person per year. That's new: FINRA raised it from one hundred in March twenty twenty-six, and the M S R B matched it in June. Older study material still says one hundred. Business entertainment where you're actually there doesn't count toward the limit.

stem: Under MSRB Rule G-37, a municipal finance professional may contribute up to what amount per election to an official of an issuer, for whom the professional is entitled to vote, without triggering the two-year ban on municipal securities business?
spoken_stem: Under M S R B Rule G thirty-seven, how much per election can a municipal finance professional give to an issuer official they can vote for, without triggering the two-year business ban? A, one hundred. B, two hundred fifty. C, one thousand. D, twenty-five hundred.
explanation: B is correct. G-37 allows contributions up to $250 per election to an issuer official for whom the municipal finance professional is entitled to vote. Larger contributions can trigger a two-year ban on negotiated municipal securities business with that issuer. A is wrong: $100 was the old MSRB gift limit, which is $300 for FINRA-member dealers since June 2026. C and D are not G-37 figures.
spoken_explanation: B, two hundred fifty dollars per election, and only if you can vote for that official. Go over, and the firm can face a two-year ban on doing business with that issuer. The rule is meant to stop pay-to-play: firms giving to officials who then pick them to underwrite bonds. Contributions are tracked on M S R B Form G thirty-seven.

stem: A college student passes the SIE but does not join a FINRA member firm right away. For how long are her SIE results valid?

choices.text: 2 years
4 years
5 years
Indefinitely

spoken_stem: A college student passes the SIE but does not join a FINRA member firm right away. For how long are her SIE results valid? A, 2 years. B, 4 years. C, 5 years. D, Indefinitely.
explanation: B is correct. SIE results are valid for four years from the date the candidate passes. She can pass the SIE without firm sponsorship, but to register she must also pass a representative-level exam, such as the Series 7, while associated with a member firm within that window. A is the general lapse period for registrations of people who leave the industry. C relates to the Maintaining Qualifications Program. D is wrong.
spoken_explanation: B is correct. SIE results are valid for four years from the date the candidate passes. She can pass the SIE without firm sponsorship, but to register she must also pass a representative-level exam, such as the Series 7, while associated with a member firm within that window. A is the general lapse period for registrations of people who leave the industry. C relates to the Maintaining Qualifications Program. D is wrong.

stem: Which statement about passing the SIE is TRUE?

choices.text: It alone qualifies a person to sell securities
It replaces the Series 63 state exam
It requires sponsorship by a member firm
It is a corequisite; the candidate must also pass a representative-level exam and be associated with a member firm to register

spoken_stem: Which statement about passing the SIE is TRUE? A, It alone qualifies a person to sell securities. B, It replaces the Series 63 state exam. C, It requires sponsorship by a member firm. D, It is a corequisite, the candidate must also pass a representative-level exam and be associated with a member firm to register.
explanation: D is correct. The SIE is a general knowledge corequisite. To become registered, a person must also pass a qualification exam such as the Series 6 or 7, which requires member firm sponsorship, and be associated with a member. A is wrong because the SIE alone permits no securities business. C is wrong because anyone 18 or older can take the SIE without sponsorship. B is wrong because state law exams like the Series 63 are separate.
spoken_explanation: D is correct. The SIE is a general knowledge corequisite. To become registered, a person must also pass a qualification exam such as the Series 6 or 7, which requires member firm sponsorship, and be associated with a member. A is wrong because the SIE alone permits no securities business. C is wrong because anyone 18 or older can take the SIE without sponsorship. B is wrong because state law exams like the Series 63 are separate.

stem: A registered representative leaves the industry and does not elect to participate in the Maintaining Qualifications Program. Generally, after how long will he have to requalify by exam to register again?

choices.text: 6 months
1 year
2 years
10 years

spoken_stem: A registered representative leaves the industry and does not elect to participate in the Maintaining Qualifications Program. Generally, after how long will he have to requalify by exam to register again? A, 6 months. B, 1 year. C, 2 years. D, 10 years.
explanation: C is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1210, a person whose registration has been terminated for two or more years generally must requalify by exam. The Maintaining Qualifications Program lets eligible people extend that window to up to five years by completing annual continuing education. A, B and D are not the standard lapse period. This is separate from the four-year validity of SIE results.
spoken_explanation: C is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1210, a person whose registration has been terminated for two or more years generally must requalify by exam. The Maintaining Qualifications Program lets eligible people extend that window to up to five years by completing annual continuing education. A, B and D are not the standard lapse period. This is separate from the four-year validity of SIE results.

stem: Under the Maintaining Qualifications Program, a person who leaves the industry can keep their qualification status valid for up to five years by:

choices.text: Paying an annual FINRA fee only
Completing annual continuing education
Retaking the SIE every year
Remaining a customer of a member firm

spoken_stem: Under the Maintaining Qualifications Program, a person who leaves the industry can keep their qualification status valid for up to five years by: A, Paying an annual FINRA fee only. B, Completing annual continuing education. C, Retaking the SIE every year. D, Remaining a customer of a member firm.
explanation: B is correct. The Maintaining Qualifications Program, part of FINRA Rule 1240, lets eligible individuals who terminate a registration maintain their qualifications for up to five years by completing continuing education each year. Without it, qualifications generally lapse after two years. A, C and D aren't how the program works.
spoken_explanation: B is correct. The Maintaining Qualifications Program, part of FINRA Rule 1240, lets eligible individuals who terminate a registration maintain their qualifications for up to five years by completing continuing education each year. Without it, qualifications generally lapse after two years. A, C and D aren't how the program works.

stem: A registered representative fails to complete the annual Regulatory Element by December 31. What is the consequence?

choices.text: The rep becomes CE inactive and may not perform activities requiring registration or receive compensation for them until it's completed
A $1,000 fine only
The rep's registration is immediately and permanently revoked
There is no consequence until a second year is missed

spoken_stem: A registered representative fails to complete the annual Regulatory Element by December 31. What is the consequence? A, The rep becomes CE inactive and may not perform activities requiring registration or receive compensation for them until it's completed. B, A 1,000 dollars fine only. C, The rep's registration is immediately and permanently revoked. D, There is no consequence until a second year is missed.
explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1240, a person who misses the Regulatory Element deadline is designated CE inactive. Until the requirement is satisfied, the person can't perform, or be compensated for, any activity requiring registration. If the person stays CE inactive for two consecutive years, the registration is administratively terminated. B, C and D misstate the consequence.
spoken_explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1240, a person who misses the Regulatory Element deadline is designated CE inactive. Until the requirement is satisfied, the person can't perform, or be compensated for, any activity requiring registration. If the person stays CE inactive for two consecutive years, the registration is administratively terminated. B, C and D misstate the consequence.

stem: The Firm Element of continuing education is BEST described as:

choices.text: Annual training developed by the member firm based on a needs analysis of its covered persons
A FINRA-administered computer exam taken every three years
Training required only for principals
Optional training that has no rule basis

spoken_stem: The Firm Element of continuing education is BEST described as: A, Annual training developed by the member firm based on a needs analysis of its covered persons. B, A FINRA-administered computer exam taken every three years. C, Training required only for principals. D, Optional training that has no rule basis.
explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1240, each member firm must maintain a continuing education program for its covered registered persons. The program is based on an annual needs analysis and written training plan, covering topics like products, services and regulatory concerns relevant to their roles. B wrongly describes the Regulatory Element, which is FINRA-delivered and annual. C and D are wrong because Firm Element applies broadly and is required.
spoken_explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA Rule 1240, each member firm must maintain a continuing education program for its covered registered persons. The program is based on an annual needs analysis and written training plan, covering topics like products, services and regulatory concerns relevant to their roles. B wrongly describes the Regulatory Element, which is FINRA-delivered and annual. C and D are wrong because Firm Element applies broadly and is required.

stem: Under SEC Rule 17f-2, which broker-dealer employee generally must be fingerprinted?

choices.text: Only registered representatives
Only employees who work on the trading floor
Only principals
Partners, directors, officers and employees, including those who handle funds or securities or have access to records, subject to limited exceptions

spoken_stem: Under SEC Rule 17f-2, which broker-dealer employee generally must be fingerprinted? A, Only registered representatives. B, Only employees who work on the trading floor. C, Only principals. D, Partners, directors, officers and employees, including those who handle funds or securities or have access to records, subject to limited exceptions.
explanation: D is correct. SEC Rule 17f-2 requires broker-dealers to fingerprint their partners, directors, officers and employees, with limited exceptions for people who don't sell securities, don't handle funds or securities, and don't have access to original books and records. Fingerprints are submitted to the FBI through FINRA for a criminal background check. A, C and B are too narrow.
spoken_explanation: D is correct. SEC Rule 17f-2 requires broker-dealers to fingerprint their partners, directors, officers and employees, with limited exceptions for people who don't sell securities, don't handle funds or securities, and don't have access to original books and records. Fingerprints are submitted to the FBI through FINRA for a criminal background check. A, C and B are too narrow.

stem: Under FINRA Rule 3110(e), before applying to register a new person, a member firm must:

choices.text: Rely solely on the applicant's own statements
Investigate the applicant's good character, business reputation, qualifications and experience
Obtain FINRA's prior approval of the hire
Wait 90 days after the hire

spoken_stem: Under FINRA Rule 3110(e), before applying to register a new person, a member firm must: A, Rely solely on the applicant's own statements. B, Investigate the applicant's good character, business reputation, qualifications and experience. C, Obtain FINRA's prior approval of the hire. D, Wait 90 days after the hire.
explanation: B is correct. Rule 3110(e) requires the firm to ascertain, through investigation, the good character, business reputation, qualifications and experience of an applicant before applying for registration. Firms must also verify the Form U4 information, including a public records search for items like judgments, liens and bankruptcies, within 30 calendar days after filing. A is insufficient. C and D aren't requirements.
spoken_explanation: B is correct. Rule 3110(e) requires the firm to ascertain, through investigation, the good character, business reputation, qualifications and experience of an applicant before applying for registration. Firms must also verify the Form U4 information, including a public records search for items like judgments, liens and bankruptcies, within 30 calendar days after filing. A is insufficient. C and D aren't requirements.

stem: Which of the following events would MOST likely make a person subject to statutory disqualification?

choices.text: A misdemeanor conviction for embezzlement 4 years ago
A misdemeanor conviction for disorderly conduct 2 years ago
A civil lawsuit by a neighbor that was dismissed
A tax lien that was paid off

spoken_stem: Which of the following events would MOST likely make a person subject to statutory disqualification? A, A misdemeanor conviction for embezzlement 4 years ago. B, A misdemeanor conviction for disorderly conduct 2 years ago. C, A civil lawsuit by a neighbor that was dismissed. D, A tax lien that was paid off.
explanation: A is correct. Statutory disqualification under Exchange Act Section 3(a)(39) includes any felony conviction within 10 years and misdemeanor convictions within 10 years involving securities, embezzlement, fraud, theft, bribery, perjury and similar conduct. B is a misdemeanor unrelated to investments or dishonesty. C is a dismissed civil matter. D may need to be disclosed on a U4 if unsatisfied, but it isn't a disqualification.
spoken_explanation: A is correct. Statutory disqualification under Exchange Act Section 3(a)(39) includes any felony conviction within 10 years and misdemeanor convictions within 10 years involving securities, embezzlement, fraud, theft, bribery, perjury and similar conduct. stem: A member firm's compliance analyst does not need a registration for her job but wants to keep her Series 7 qualification active. Under FINRA Rule 1210, the firm may:

choices.text: Not register her under any circumstances
Permissively register her
Register her only if she solicits customers
Register her only with the SEC

spoken_stem: A member firm's compliance analyst does not need a registration for her job but wants to keep her Series 7 qualification active. Under FINRA Rule 1210, the firm may: A, Not register her under any circumstances. B, Permissively register her. C, Register her only if she solicits customers. D, Register her only with the SEC.
explanation: B is correct. Rule 1210 allows permissive registrations, which let a firm register associated persons who are not required to be registered, such as people in administrative or compliance roles. That keeps their qualifications active, and they're subject to all the rules that apply to registered persons. A is wrong because permissive registration is allowed. C is wrong because she'd then be required to register. D is wrong because individual representatives register through FINRA's system.
spoken_explanation: B is correct. Rule 1210 allows permissive registrations, which let a firm register associated persons who are not required to be registered, such as people in administrative or compliance roles. That keeps their qualifications active, and they're subject to all the rules that apply to registered persons. A is wrong because permissive registration is allowed. C is wrong because she'd then be required to register. D is wrong because individual representatives register through FINRA's system.

stem: As of November 2026, a candidate fails the SIE for the second time. How long must the candidate wait before retaking it?

choices.text: 30 days
15 days
No wait
180 days

spoken_stem: As of November 2026, a candidate fails the SIE for the second time. How long must the candidate wait before retaking it? A, 30 days. B, 15 days. C, No wait. D, 180 days.
explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA's current rules, as of November 2026, candidates must wait 30 days after a first or second failed attempt and 180 days after a third or later failure. FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-18 reduces these waits to 15 days after the first and second failures and 60 days after the third, effective January 19, 2027. So B will become correct for retakes after that date. C and D aren't the current second-attempt waits.
spoken_explanation: A is correct. Under FINRA's current rules, as of November 2026, candidates must wait 30 days after a first or second failed attempt and 180 days after a third or later failure. FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-18 reduces these waits to 15 days after the first and second failures and 60 days after the third, effective January 19, 2027. So B will become correct for retakes after that date. C and D aren't the current second-attempt waits.

stem: A registered representative located in New York wants to solicit a customer who lives in New Jersey. In addition to FINRA registration, the rep generally must:

choices.text: Do nothing more
Obtain the customer's waiver
Be registered as an agent in New Jersey
Register with the SEC individually

spoken_stem: A registered representative located in New York wants to solicit a customer who lives in New Jersey. In addition to FINRA registration, the rep generally must: A, Do nothing more. B, Obtain the customer's waiver. C, Be registered as an agent in New Jersey. D, Register with the SEC individually.
explanation: C is correct. State blue-sky laws generally require agents to be registered in the state where the customer resides before soliciting or effecting transactions there, subject to limited exemptions. Passing the Series 63 or 66 is usually required for agent registration. A ignores state law. B is wrong because customers can't waive state registration. D is wrong because individual reps don't register separately with the SEC.
spoken_explanation: C is correct. State blue-sky laws generally require agents to be registered in the state where the customer resides before soliciting or effecting transactions there, subject to limited exemptions. Passing the Series 63 or 66 is usually required for agent registration. A ignores state law. B is wrong because customers can't waive state registration. D is wrong because individual reps don't register separately with the SEC.

stem: Once a candidate is enrolled for a FINRA qualification exam, the window within which the exam must be taken is generally:

choices.text: 30 days
60 days
120 days
1 year

spoken_stem: Once a candidate is enrolled for a FINRA qualification exam, the window within which the exam must be taken is generally: A, 30 days. B, 60 days. C, 120 days. D, 1 year.
explanation: C is correct. A FINRA exam enrollment generally opens a 120-day window during which the candidate must schedule and sit for the exam. If the window expires, the candidate must re-enroll and pay again. A, B and D are not the standard window. The fee for the SIE is set by FINRA, and firms often pay for representative exams.
spoken_explanation: C is correct. A FINRA exam enrollment generally opens a 120-day window during which the candidate must schedule and sit for the exam. If the window expires, the candidate must re-enroll and pay again. A, B and D are not the standard window. The fee for the SIE is set by FINRA, and firms often pay for representative exams.

stem: True or false: A representative may tell customers that being registered with FINRA means FINRA has approved her abilities and endorses her recommendations.

choices.text: True
False

spoken_stem: True or false: A representative may tell customers that being registered with FINRA means FINRA has approved her abilities and endorses her recommendations.
explanation: False. FINRA Rule 1122 and SEC Rule 15c1-3 prohibit misleading statements about membership or registration. Registration means only that the person met the qualification requirements. It doesn't mean any regulator approves of the person's skill, character or recommendations. Implying endorsement is a misrepresentation that can lead to discipline.
spoken_explanation: False. FINRA Rule 1122 and SEC Rule 15c1-3 prohibit misleading statements about membership or registration. Registration means only that the person met the qualification requirements. It doesn't mean any regulator approves of the person's skill, character or recommendations. Implying endorsement is a misrepresentation that can lead to discipline.

stem: True or false: A person subject to statutory disqualification can never associate with a FINRA member under any circumstances.

choices.text: True
False

spoken_stem: True or false: A person subject to statutory disqualification can never associate with a FINRA member under any circumstances.
explanation: False. A statutorily disqualified person may be able to associate with a member firm if the firm files an eligibility application, often called a Membership Continuance Application, and FINRA approves it. Approval often comes with heightened supervision conditions. Without approval, the firm can't let that person associate with it. The burden is on the firm to show the association is in the public interest.
spoken_explanation: False. A statutorily disqualified person may be able to associate with a member firm if the firm files an eligibility application, often called a Membership Continuance Application, and FINRA approves it. Approval often comes with heightened supervision conditions. Without approval, the firm can't let that person associate with it. stem: Form U4 requires a candidate to provide which of the following?

choices.text: Five years of employment history and three years of residential history
Only the current employer
Ten years of employment history and five years of residential history
A full credit report

spoken_stem: Form U4 requires a candidate to provide which of the following? A, Five years of employment history and three years of residential history. B, Only the current employer. C, Ten years of employment history and five years of residential history. D, A full credit report.
explanation: C is correct. Form U4 asks for 10 years of employment history and 5 years of residential history, plus disclosure questions covering criminal matters, regulatory actions, civil judicial actions, customer complaints, terminations and financial matters such as bankruptcies, liens and judgments. A has the periods wrong. B is incomplete. D is wrong because the firm may run its own checks, but the U4 is the disclosure form.

stem: Who signs the Form U4?

choices.text: Only the candidate
Only the firm's CEO
Only FINRA
Both the candidate and an appropriate principal of the firm

spoken_stem: Who signs the Form U4? A, Only the candidate. B, Only the firm's CEO. C, Only FINRA. D, Both the candidate and an appropriate principal of the firm.
explanation: D is correct. The candidate attests that the information is accurate and complete. That attestation includes agreeing to arbitrate disputes as required by SRO rules. A principal of the member firm also signs, certifying that the firm has taken appropriate steps to verify the information. A, C and B are incomplete or incorrect. Filing false information is a serious violation for both the individual and the firm.
spoken_explanation: D is correct. The candidate attests that the information is accurate and complete. That attestation includes agreeing to arbitrate disputes as required by SRO rules. stem: Under FINRA rules, which of the following is a written customer complaint?

An email from a customer alleging that her rep made unauthorized trades
A customer's verbal request to close an account
A rep's notes about a customer's tone

explanation: B is correct. FINRA Rule 4513 defines a written customer complaint as any written grievance, including electronic communications, from a customer or someone acting for the customer, involving the activities of the firm or its associated persons in connection with securities. A and C are oral, and D isn't from the customer. Oral complaints should still be handled under firm procedures, but they aren't written complaints for these record and reporting rules.

stem: Under FINRA Rule 4513, a member must keep records of written customer complaints at the office of supervisory jurisdiction for at least:

explanation: A is correct. Rule 4513 requires each member to keep a record of every written customer complaint for at least four years. The record covers the complainant, the date, the associated person involved, a description of the complaint, and any action taken, and it's kept at the office of supervisory jurisdiction responsible for that office. C and B are too short. D is the period for certain other records, such as blotters.

explanation: C is correct. stem: Which of the following is a potential red flag that a firm's supervisor should investigate?

A customer requests quarterly statements

explanation: C is correct. Customer funds should be payable to the firm or clearing firm, never to the rep personally. stem: A representative takes a client's portfolio manager to a $450 dinner and a baseball game, and attends both with him. Under FINRA Rule 3220, this is:

explanation: D is correct. Ordinary and usual business entertainment, like a meal or sporting event where the member's representative is present, isn't counted toward the gift limit, provided it isn't so frequent or extensive as to raise questions of propriety. A violation regardless of value
Exempt because tickets are entertainment
A gift valued at $240, within the $300 annual limit if no other gifts were given

explanation: D is correct. When the rep doesn't attend, tickets are a gift, not entertainment. Tickets are valued at the higher of cost or face value, so two $120 tickets equal $240. The annual limit per recipient is $300 under Rule 3220 as amended effective March 30, 2026, so this fits if nothing else was given that year. A wrongly values each ticket separately instead of aggregating. C applies only when the rep is present. B is wrong.

stem: A mutual fund sponsor wants to pay for a training meeting for a broker-dealer's reps. Under FINRA's non-cash compensation rules, which condition applies?

choices.text: Attendance can be a reward for meeting sales targets
The sponsor may also pay for the reps' spouses
The firm must approve attendance, and attendance can't be conditioned on achieving sales targets
The meeting can be at any luxury resort

spoken_stem: A mutual fund sponsor wants to pay for a training meeting for a broker-dealer's reps. Under FINRA's non-cash compensation rules, which condition applies? A, Attendance can be a reward for meeting sales targets. B, The sponsor may also pay for the reps' spouses. C, The firm must approve attendance, and attendance can't be conditioned on achieving sales targets. D, The meeting can be at any luxury resort.
explanation: C is correct. The non-cash compensation rules, Rules 2341(l)(5), 2320(g)(4), 2310(c) and 5110(h), allow product sponsors to pay for training or education meetings only if the member approves attendance, attendance isn't conditioned on sales, the location is appropriate for the purpose, and the sponsor doesn't pay for guests. A, B and D violate those conditions. Gifts from sponsors are separately capped at $300 per person per year as of 2026.
spoken_explanation: C is correct. The non-cash compensation rules, Rules 2341(l)(5), 2320(g)(4), 2310(c) and 5110(h), allow product sponsors to pay for training or education meetings only if the member approves attendance, attendance isn't conditioned on sales, the location is appropriate for the purpose, and the sponsor doesn't pay for guests. A, B and D violate those conditions. Gifts from sponsors are separately capped at 300 dollars per person per year as of 2026.

stem: A municipal finance professional at a dealer contributes $1,000 to the campaign of a city mayor who can influence the award of the city's bond business. The professional lives in that city. Under MSRB Rule G-37, the MOST likely consequence is:

choices.text: Nothing, since he can vote for the mayor
The contribution must be reported only on his tax return
He must resign immediately
His firm is generally banned from negotiated municipal securities business with the city for two years

spoken_stem: A municipal finance professional at a dealer contributes 1,000 dollars to the campaign of a city mayor who can influence the award of the city's bond business. The professional lives in that city. Under MSRB Rule G-37, the MOST likely consequence is: A, Nothing, since he can vote for the mayor. B, The contribution must be reported only on his tax return. C, He must resign immediately. D, His firm is generally banned from negotiated municipal securities business with the city for two years.
explanation: D is correct. G-37's exemption covers only contributions of up to $250 per election to officials the professional is entitled to vote for. A $1,000 contribution exceeds that, which generally triggers a two-year ban on the dealer engaging in negotiated municipal securities business with that issuer. A ignores the $250 cap. C and B aren't the rule. Firms also disclose contributions on Form G-37.
spoken_explanation: D is correct. G-37's exemption covers only contributions of up to 250 dollars per election to officials the professional is entitled to vote for. A 1,000 dollars contribution exceeds that, which generally triggers a two-year ban on the dealer engaging in negotiated municipal securities business with that issuer. A ignores the 250 dollars cap. stem: Under FINRA Rule 3270, which outside activity requires prior written notice to the member firm?

Coaching a child's soccer team without pay
Managing one's own personal checking account
Serving as a paid director of a local company

explanation: D is correct. Rule 3270 requires prior written notice for outside business activities where the person is an employee, independent contractor, sole proprietor, officer, director or partner of another person, or is compensated or reasonably expects compensation. stem: A rep wants to help a friend's startup sell shares to a few investors but will receive no compensation. Under FINRA Rule 3280, the rep must:

choices.text: Do nothing because no compensation is involved
Obtain FINRA approval
Give the firm prior written notice describing the transaction and his role
Become a partner in the startup first

spoken_stem: A rep wants to help a friend's startup sell shares to a few investors but will receive no compensation. D, Become a partner in the startup first.
explanation: C is correct. For a private securities transaction without compensation, Rule 3280 still requires prior written notice to the firm describing the proposed transaction and the person's role. The firm must acknowledge it in writing and may require adherence to specified conditions. If compensation were involved, the firm would have to approve or disapprove and supervise it if approved. A, B and D are wrong. Rule 3290 replaces Rule 3280 effective October 25, 2027.

spoken_stem: A broker-dealer acts as transfer agent for an issuer and uses the shareholder list it maintains to solicit purchases of other securities. Under FINRA Rule 2060, this is: A, Permitted for any purpose. B, Prohibited unless the issuer requests and authorizes the use. C, Permitted if customers are charged reduced commissions. D, Required by the issuer.
explanation: B is correct. Rule 2060 prohibits a member that receives information in a fiduciary capacity, such as acting as transfer agent or trustee, from using it to solicit purchases, sales or exchanges of securities, unless the issuer specifically requests and authorizes it. A, C and D ignore the prohibition. It protects issuers and their shareholders from misuse of confidential information.

spoken_stem: True or false: Under FINRA Rule 3220, gifts given in relation to the business of the recipient's employer are aggregated per recipient on an annual basis for the 300 dollars limit.
explanation: True. The $300 limit, effective March 30, 2026, applies per recipient per year. All gifts to the same person in relation to the employer's business during the year are added together. Firms must track and record gifts to check compliance, and their procedures must say whether they track by calendar year, fiscal year or on a rolling basis. Personal gifts unrelated to business, such as a wedding gift, aren't counted.

explanation: True. Under Rule 3270, the firm must consider whether the activity will interfere with or otherwise compromise the person's responsibilities to the firm or its customers. It must also consider whether customers or the public might view it as part of the firm's business. The firm may impose conditions or prohibit the activity, and it must keep a record of its decision.
